Introduction to Nanotechnology
1. Introduction
Nanotechnology refers to science and engineering at the nanoscale.

Materials with dimensions
between 1 and 100 nanometers are called nanomaterials.

Nanomaterials behave differently from bulk
materials because of their extremely small size.

Surface-to-Volume Ratio
As particle size decreases, the surface-to-volume ratio increases significantly.

A larger percentage of
atoms remain on the surface of the material.

This changes the chemical reactivity and physical
properties of nanomaterials.

Quantum Confinement
Quantum confinement affects the electronic behavior of nanomaterials.

The density of states changes
when dimensions become extremely small.
This results in unique optical and electrical properties.

Applications of Nanotechnology
Nanotechnology is used in medicine, electronics, energy storage, and sensors.

Nanoparticles are used
in drug delivery and cancer therapy.

Nanomaterials are also used in solar cells and water purification
systems.
